# Audio direction

Everything you hear and how it is made. Read before adding, retuning or wiring any sound.
Code: `tools/audio/` (Python 2.7, standard library + PIL), `Sounds`, `Voice`, `VoiceMakerScreen`,
`SettingsScreen`.

**In one line:** every sound, ambience and music loop is generated by code in `tools/audio/`,
never recorded or hand-edited - except a kid's own recording of their pet. A pet's voice is the
kid's: a base sound reshaped with sliders, or their own recording, and the game varies it every
time the pet talks.

## The sound of the game

A kid's drawing come to life, so a soft cartoon:
- **Drawing** sounds like paper: a crayon that scratches only while it moves (louder when faster),
  an eraser rub, a bloop-splosh for the paint bucket, a scrunched-up page for Clear.
- **Pets** pat about on padded feet pitched by size (a mouse patters, a dinosaur thumps), boing
  when they hop, flutter when they fly, bloop when they swim, crunch when they eat, snore asleep.
- **Rewards** are little bells. Everything tonal is in **C major**, the key of all three music
  loops, so a chime always agrees with whatever is playing.
- **Every button** taps softly by itself (`Sounds` connects every BaseButton as it appears), so
  no screen has to remember to.
- **Places** each have a quiet bed: birds, surf, wind, bubbles, drips, crickets, a hum on the
  Moon, a music box in Candy Land.

## Pet voices (built)

A pet's voice is a **recipe** (`Voice`): a base sound, or the kid's own recording, plus sliders.

| control | what it does | the pictures at each end |
|---|---|---|
| base | 18 sounds: bark, meow, chirp, squeak, moo, roar, hoot, ribbit, quack, oink, baa, trumpet, purr, beep, gurgle, boing, trill, honk - or "Mine" | each a face making its noise |
| pitch | ±12 semitones, without changing the length | whale / little bird |
| speed | half to double, without changing the pitch | turtle / rabbit |
| wobble | vibrato | flat line / wavy line |
| echo | three repeats, fading | flat line / mountain |
| bend | the pitch sliding up to 7 semitones down or up across the sound | slide down / ski jump |
| robot | ring modulation | flat line / robot |
| backwards | plays it in reverse | rewind |

`Voice.render` does the work in GDScript, because the samples must be readable: a time stretch
(four overlapping grains, each lined up with what is already there, so they add rather than
cancel), then a variable-rate resample for pitch, bend and wobble, then robot and echo.
Separate pitch and speed come from stretching by pitch/speed and resampling by pitch.

**The bases are raw float files** (`sfx/voices/*.f32`, mono, 22050 Hz), not WAVs: Godot
compresses imported WAVs (QOA), and compressed audio cannot be read back as samples. The export
preset must include `*.f32` (see `android.md`).

**Variation (decided).** A pet never makes exactly the same noise twice. `Voice.speak` plays its
sound 1-3 times ("yip yip yip"), each repeat one of three versions with the sliders nudged a
little (`Voice.NUDGES`: about ±0.7 semitones, ±6% speed, a touch of bend or wobble), then a ±5%
pitch on top, a small volume change and an uneven gap. Happy hearts are a little higher,
celebrating stars higher still and longer, a question bends up, and the yawn before a nap is a
slow low version. Repeats are capped so the whole thing stays under about 2.4 seconds. Its mouth
opens for each one. Versions are rendered once and cached.

**Where voices come from.** A new pet starts with a guess from its size and parts (wings chirp,
fins gurgle) and the kid shapes it in creation's "What does it sound like?" step, or later from
the pet panel's Voice button or Fix. Adoptable pets and rivals have preset recipes
(`Adoptables.VOICES`, `Rivals.VOICES`). **Drawn toys** can have a sound too (optional, from the
same screen), played when they bounce, are caught or squeak.

## The microphone - optional (decided)

- Off until turned on: in Settings, or the first time a kid taps Record, with a plain yes/no that
  says the sound stays on the device. "No thanks" always works; every mic feature has a touch way
  round it (pick a base sound).
- Android asks for `RECORD_AUDIO` only then, not at install.
- **A recording is at most 3 seconds** (`Sounds.MAX_RECORD`), with a filling bar and auto-stop.
  It is made mono at 22050 Hz, the silence before and after cut, and evened out; too quiet and the
  kid is asked to try again.
- Stored as `voice.f32` in the pet's folder (`sound.f32` for a toy). **Never uploaded, never
  shared** (`sharing.md`).
- Loudness and playback only - no speech recognition (no AI).

## Loudness follows how often a sound plays

Every effect is normalised to its peak in `REGISTRY` (`tools/audio/sfx.py`) and played at unity.
**The registry is the mix.** Change balance there, not with volume at call sites.

| how often | peak dBFS | members |
|---|---|---|
| once in a while | -4 to -9 | fanfare, adopt, count_go, level_up, trust_up, buy, star, build, cheer |
| now and then | -10 to -14 | munch, squeak, trampoline, splash, splat, shake, clean, catch, good, place, throw, done, fill |
| often | -15 to -20 | bounce, hop, heart, sniff, snore, flap, scrub, brush, the crayon and eraser loops |
| constantly | -21 and below | ui_tap (-22), step (-23), the rain loop (-25) |

Pet voices are rendered to a steady peak and play on their own bus. Ambiences peak at -20 dBFS
(steady beds lower: Moon -29, mountains -23, desert -22, beach -21) and the music at -3 dBFS.
`Sounds.BUS_TRIM` sets the buses under the kid's sliders: music -8 dB, ambience -3 dB, voices -1
dB, so a "full" music slider still sits under everything else. A hard limiter at -1 dBFS guards
the SFX bus.

## Music

`tools/audio/music.py`, on `band.py` (DrawFight's instruments and sequencer). Mono, 22050 Hz,
seamless loops.

- **home** - 100 BPM, swung: a strummed ukulele, a walking bass, snaps and a shaker, a whistled
  tune, a toy piano answering. C - Am - F - G with secondary dominants (E7, D7), a borrowed F minor
  wink in the bridge, ending on G7 into the top. Homes, shop, calendar, settings.
- **create** - 84 BPM, straight: a slow toy-piano tune over plucked ukulele arpeggios, no drums.
  Drawing, fixing, making things and voices.
- **contest** - 152 BPM: a handheld-console lead calling, cartoon horns answering, offbeat chops,
  a bouncing bass, claps, a slide whistle back to the top. Competitions.

`GameRoot._music_for` crossfades the right one in as screens change, and a home's place
ambience under it.

## Building and checking

```
python tools/audio/build.py --all --sheet
"$GODOT_BIN" --headless --path . --import
```

Nobody on this project can hear the output, so `--sheet` draws every sound as a waveform over a
spectrogram (`.shots/sound_<kind>.png`): a rising pitch is a rising line, a wobble a wave, an echo
a repeat. `tools/voice_check.gd` renders one base through every slider into
`.shots/voice_check/` and `tools/audio/sheet.py` draws them - the check that "higher" really moves
the bands up at the same length, and "faster" really shortens at the same pitch. `Sounds` prints
how many effects loaded and warns about any missing.
